ticket.title: miter find: AST-aware literal/regex search that returns enclosing symbols and per-crate counts
acceptance_criteria:
Implemented and verified 2026-11-06 (commit 1d9c86a, miter).

miter find <PATTERN> [--ignore-case] [--max N] [--json] reports every hit in the files the index knows about, each attributed to its enclosing declaration via the same span arithmetic GB-279 landed, in reverse. Text form prints file:line:column, the enclosing path, the source line, and a per-crate breakdown.

Live: find SpanGuard --max 3 -> 3 hits in 2 files, by crate gaugeblock-workspace=3; hits on a re-export line and two doc comments were correctly marked '(outside any declaration)' rather than dropped.

Design decisions, each refusing a confident-but-wrong answer:
- --ignore-case folds ASCII only, because to_ascii_lowercase preserves byte length while general Unicode folding does not. An offset into a differently-sized folded string would attribute hits to the wrong declaration.
- Hits outside any declaration are reported, not filtered: a literal in a mod.rs re-export list is still a hit, and hiding it would make the count disagree with what the reader finds.
- Indexed files that can no longer be read are counted in the output instead of skipped silently.
- --max defaults to 100 and the output says when it stopped early.

Regex search is deliberately not included: no regex crate is in miter's dependency graph, and adding one to unblock a flag needs to be a decision rather than a side effect. Filed as a follow-up.

Tier 2: fmt clean, clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean, 7 find+enclosing tests green, docs check 9 present 0 missing 0 drifted, audit no file over 250 in miter.

task.title: miter find: AST-aware literal/regex search that returns enclosing symbols and per-crate counts

acceptance_criteria: EVIDENCE 2026-11-06: across a long session I ran well over a hundred shell searches and used miter's CLI only for deps/contracts
essentially never its symbol tools. The reason is query shape
not preference: most questions were literal or aggregate - which files contain  and how many per repo
which TOML configs carry
which Markdown mentions a subcommand
where does the string 'manual' appear - and miter has no literal search.\n\nPROPOSED: 'miter find <regex>' over indexed sources returning hits grouped by enclosing symbol with file:line
plus a per-crate count summary. That single command subsumes most of the grep calls: the count answers 'how widespread'
the enclosing symbol answers 'where do I edit'
and both come from the index rather than a text scan. --text flag to include non-indexed files (TOML
MD) so one tool covers both worlds instead of leaving a documented boundary agents will forget.\n\nACCEPTANCE: for a literal present in N symbols across M crates
one invocation returns all N with enclosing symbols and the per-crate counts; output is stable enough to diff between runs
and cheap enough that an agent prefers it to grep.
TEXT CORRECTION: the previous criterion lost two terms to shell interpolation - backticks inside a double-quoted argument are executed by zsh

so the words Command::new and verification_commands were replaced by empty output. Reinstated here with single quotes. The substance stands: most of my queries were literal or aggregate (files containing a process spawn
how many per repo; TOML configs carrying a verification key; Markdown naming a subcommand; where a string literal appears)
and miter has no literal search
so grep was the only tool that could answer.

DEPENDENCY found 2026-11-06: both this and GB-279 need declaration END lines persisted, which miter does not store today (declarations are keyed file:line:name). 'find' returning an enclosing symbol has the same requirement as 'enclosing' itself - otherwise the grouping is approximate and silently wrong.

Cheapest path: extend the symbol record with end_line (and depth if cheap) at index time, one migration, then build find and enclosing on top of it together. Doing either alone re-opens the schema.
